desc:
Replace Your Exploit-Ridden Firmware with Linux - Ronald Minnich, Google

With the WikiLeaks release of the vault7 material, the security of the UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) firmware used in most PCs and laptops is once again a concern. UEFI is a proprietary and closed-source operating system, with a codebase almost as large as the Linux kernel, that runs when the system is powered

There's a great talk on the risks posed by the capabilities of these security coprocessors by an extremely well-versed individual at Google who was (leading? involved at a high level?) working on Google's efforts to neutralize these dangerous subsystems at Embedded Linux Con in 2017: [link]
